facts.statement: Monolophosaurus is an extinct tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic found in what is now Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: Monolophosaurus ( ; meaning "single-crested lizard") is an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shishugou Formation in what is now Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was named for the single crest located on top of its skull.
facts.quote: It was named for the single crest on top of its skull.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus was a mid-sized theropod measuring approximately 5 to 5.5 meters in length and weighing 475 kilograms.
facts.quote: Monolophosaurus was a mid-sized theropod at about 5 - 5.5 m long and weighed 475 kg.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton was discovered by Dong Zhiming in 1981 during oil industry exploration.
facts.quote: A nearly complete skeleton of a theropod new to science was discovered by Dong Zhiming in 1981, during stratigraphic exploration for the benefit of the oil industry.

facts.statement: The fossil was not unearthed until 1984.
facts.quote: The fossil was not unearthed until 1984.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the Junggar Basin within layers of the Wucaiwan Formation dating from the Bathonian-Callovian.
facts.quote: The holotype IVPP 84019 was discovered in the Junggar Basin, in layers of the Wucaiwan Formation dating from the Bathonian-Callovian.

facts.statement: The holotype represents an adult or subadult individual.
facts.quote: It represents an adult or subadult individual.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 5.5 meters and the weight at 475 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Paul estimated the length at 5.5 m and the weight at 475 kg.

facts.statement: The skull is rather flat but obscured by a large snout crest that occupies about three-quarters of the skull length and reaches the level of the eye sockets.
facts.quote: It is as such rather flat but this is obscured by the presence of a large snout crest occupying about three quarters of the skull length, reaching the level of the eye sockets.

facts.statement: CAT scans revealed that the nasal bone was heavily pneumatized with large internal air chambers.
facts.quote: CAT scans showed that internally the nasal bone is heavily pneumatised, with large air chambers.

facts.statement: The holotype shows asymmetry in tooth count, with eighteen teeth in the right dentary and seventeen in the left, a trait not rare among large theropods.
facts.quote: The holotype shows eighteen teeth in the right dentary, seventeen in the left dentary; such an asymmetry is not rare among large theropods.

facts.statement: In 2006, Thomas Carr suggested that Guanlong might be a subadult individual of Monolophosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2006, Thomas Carr suggested that Guanlong, another theropod with a large, thin, and fenestrated midline crest and from the same formation, was in fact a subadult individual of Monolophosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2010, Brusatte et al. rejected the hypothesis that Guanlong is a subadult Monolophosaurus, noting that the Guanlong holotype was a fully adult individual.
facts.quote: In 2010, Brusatte et al. rejected the identity, pointing out that the Guanlong holotype was actually a fully adult individual.

facts.statement: The praemaxilla bears four teeth while the maxilla bears thirteen teeth.
facts.quote: The praemaxilla bears four teeth. The maxilla bears thirteen teeth.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus had a vertebral column with nine neck vertebrae, fourteen back vertebrae, and five sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column consists of nine cervical vertebrae, fourteen dorsals and five sacrals.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Monolophosaurus were strongly pneumatic, featuring hollow interiors with large air chambers and side pockets.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae of the neck are strongly pneumatised. They possess pleurocoels at their sides and their insides are hollowed out by large air chambers.

facts.statement: The ilium of Monolophosaurus had a slightly convex upper profile with a front blade ending in a hook-shaped point.
facts.quote: The ilium has a slightly convex upper profile. Its front blade has a pending, hook-shaped point.

facts.statement: The pubic bones and ischia of Monolophosaurus both had a "foot" structure and were connected in pairs by bony skirts pierced by a hole.
facts.quote: The pubic bones and the ischia resemble each other in having a "foot" and being per pair connected via bony skirts, pierced by a foramen.

facts.statement: The only known individual of Monolophosaurus is estimated to be five meters long.
facts.quote: El tipo y único individuo conocido se ha estimado en cinco metros.

facts.statement: In 2016, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated Monolophosaurus to be 7.5 meters long and weigh 710 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2016, Molina-Pérez y Larramendi dieron una estimación más alta de 7,5 metros y 710 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Monolophosaurus measures 80 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo del holotipo tiene una longitud de 80 centímetros.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus had a large crest running along the midline of its snout, formed primarily by the premaxilla bone.
facts.quote: El hocico en su línea media tiene una gran cresta, cuyo frente está formado por el premaxilar.

facts.statement: The top of the Monolophosaurus crest ran parallel to the upper edge of the jaw.
facts.quote: La parte superior de la cresta corre paralela al borde superior de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Monolophosaurus features a deep groove running from an opening in the ascending ramus to an opening below the antorbital fossa.
facts.quote: El lado del premaxilar presenta un surco profundo que va desde una abertura en la rama ascendente hacia una abertura debajo de la fosa nasal.

facts.statement: The posterior ramus of the lacrimal bone in Monolophosaurus has a distinctive axe-shaped process pointing upward above the eye socket.
facts.quote: La rama posterior del lagrimal, por encima de la cuenca del ojo, tiene un proceso distintivo en forma de hacha que apunta hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The function of the unique deep groove on the premaxilla of Monolophosaurus is unknown.
facts.quote: La función de este rasgo único es desconocida.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Monolophosaurus had four teeth, while the maxilla had thirteen teeth.
facts.quote: El premaxilar tiene cuatro dientes. El maxilar tiene trece dientes.

facts.statement: In 2019, Rauhut identified Monolophosaurus as the most basal member of the Carnosauria clade.
facts.quote: In 2019, Rauhut found Monolophosaurus to be the most basal member of Carnosauria.

facts.statement: A 2023 study suggested Monolophosaurus is a sister taxon to Spinosauridae within a monophyletic Carnosauria group.
facts.quote: A 2023 examination of Irritator challengeri found Monolophosaurus to be a sister taxon to Spinosauridae as part of a larger, monophyletic Carnosauria.

facts.statement: Cau (2024) recovered Monolophosaurus as a basal member of the Allosauroidea clade.
facts.quote: Cau (2024) recovered Monolophosaurus as a basal member of Allosauroidea.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Medio

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus inhabited a warm, semi-arid environment with highly seasonal climate patterns.
facts.quote: Monolophosaurus lived in an area with a warm, semi-arid and highly seasonal climate.

facts.statement: The habitat of Monolophosaurus included numerous wetlands and well-drained distal floodplains.
facts.quote: There were many wetlands and well-drained distal floodplains.

facts.statement: The region where Monolophosaurus lived was home to conifers, ginkgos, and ferns.
facts.quote: The general area in China was home to many types of conifers, ginkgos and ferns.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Monolophosaurus shows fused fractures on its tenth and possibly eleventh neural spines.
facts.quote: The type specimen (IVPP 84019) had its tenth and possibly eleventh neural spines fractured. They are fused together.

facts.statement: Parallel ridges on the dentary of a Monolophosaurus specimen may represent tooth marks from another animal.
facts.quote: A series of parallel ridges on one of the specimen's dentaries may represent tooth marks.

facts.statement: The describers of Alpkarakush included Monolophosaurus within Spinosauridae in a 2024 phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Similarly, the describers of Alpkarakush included Monolophosaurus within Spinosauridae based on their phylogenetic analysis in 2024.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus possessed an unusually small external mandibular fenestra for a basal tetanuran.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula inferior, la fenestra mandibular externa es bastante pequeña para un tetanuro basal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Monolophosaurus has eighteen teeth in the right dentary and seventeen in the left dentary.
facts.quote: El holotipo muestra dieciocho dientes en el dentario derecho, diecisiete en el dentario izquierdo

facts.statement: A row of holes runs beneath and on the outer side of the tooth row in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Una fila de agujeros está presente debajo y en el lado externo de la fila de dientes.

facts.statement: The spine of Monolophosaurus consists of nine cervical, fourteen dorsal, and five sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral consta de nueve vértebras cervicales, catorce dorsales y cinco sacras.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Monolophosaurus are strongly pneumatized with large air chambers inside.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales del cuello están fuertemente neumatizadas.

facts.statement: The neural spines of the sacral vertebrae in Monolophosaurus do not fuse into a supraneural plate.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales de las vértebras sacras no se fusionan en una placa supraneural.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP 84019 has a fractured tenth and possibly eleventh dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, IVPP 84019, tiene fracturada la décima y posiblemente la undécima vértebra dorsal.

facts.statement: A series of parallel ridges on one dentary bone may represent tooth marks.
facts.quote: Una serie de crestas paralelas en una de los dentario de la muestra pueden representar marcas de dientes.

facts.statement: The ilium of Monolophosaurus has a slightly convex upper profile.
facts.quote: El ilion tiene un perfil superior ligeramente convexo.

facts.statement: Dong Zhiming discovered an almost complete skeleton of a new theropod in 1981 in what is now Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: Dong Zhiming descubrió un esqueleto casi completo de un terópodo nuevo para la ciencia en 1981 en lo que ahora es Xinjiang, China

facts.statement: The fossil was unearthed in 1984.
facts.quote: El fósil fue desenterrado recién en 1984.

facts.statement: In 1987, the fossil was known in the press as the invalid name Jiangjunmiaosaurus before scientific description.
facts.quote: En 1987, antes de la descripción en la literatura científica, se lo conocía en la prensa como "Jiangjunmiaosaurus", un nomen nudum inválido.

facts.statement: Zhao Xijin and Philip John Currie named and described the type species Monolophosaurus jiangi between 1993 and 1994.
facts.quote: Entre 1993 y 1994, Zhao Xijin y Philip John Currie nombraron y describieron la especie tipo Monolophosaurus jiangi.

facts.statement: The generic name Monolophosaurus derives from Greek words meaning "single" and "crest", referring to the unique crest on its snout.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego μόνος, monos, "único", y λόφος o λόφη, lophos o lophè, "cresta", en referencia a la cresta única en el hocico.

facts.statement: The specific name refers to Jiangjunmiao, an abandoned desert inn near where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se refiere a Jiangjunmiao, una posada abandonada del desierto, cerca de la cual se encontró el fósil.

facts.statement: The holotype IVPP 84019 was found in the Junggar Basin within layers of the Wucaiwan Formation dating from the Bathonian to Callovian.
facts.quote: El holotipo IVPP 84019 se descubrió en la cuenca del Junggar, en capas de la formación Wucaiwan que datan del Bathoniense al Calloviense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a fairly complete skeleton including the skull, lower jaws, spine, and pelvis.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto bastante completo que incluye el cráneo, las mandíbulas inferiores, la columna vertebral y la pelvis.

facts.statement: The posterior tail, shoulder girdle, and limbs are missing from the holotype.
facts.quote: Falta la parte posterior de la cola, la cintura escapular y las extremidades.

facts.statement: In 2010, two studies by Stephen Brusatte and colleagues redescribed the holotype, which at the time was the only known specimen.
facts.quote: En 2010, dos estudios de Stephen Brusatte y colegas redescribieron el holotipo, en ese momento todavía el único espécimen conocido, en detalle.

facts.statement: In 2006, Thomas Carr suggested that Guanlong, a theropod with a large, thin, fenestrated midline crest from the same formation, was actually a subadult Monolophosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2006, Thomas Carr sugirió que Guanlong, otro terópodo con una cresta de línea media grande, delgada y fenestrada y de la misma formación, era de hecho un individuo subadulto de Monolophosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2010, Brusatte and colleagues rejected the hypothesis that Guanlong was a subadult Monolophosaurus, noting the Guanlong holotype was actually a fully adult individual.
facts.quote: En 2010, Brusatte y colegas rechazó la identidad, señalando que el holotipo de Guanlong era en realidad un individuo completamente adulto.

facts.statement: Smith et al. in 2007 were the first to find that Monolophosaurus was a non-Neotetanuran tetanuran.
facts.quote: Smith et al. en 2007 fue la primera publicación en encontrar que Monolophosaurus era un tatanuro no Neotetanurae

facts.statement: Benson in 2008 and 2010 placed Monolophosaurus in a clade with Chuandongocoelurus that is more basal than Megalosauridae and Spinosauridae within Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: Benson en 2008 y 2010 colocó a Monolophosaurus en un clado con Chuandongocoelurus que es más basal que Megalosauridae y Spinosauridae en Megalosauroidea.

facts.statement: Later, Benson et al. in 2010 found that the Chuandongocoelurus and Monolophosaurus clade was outside Megalosauroidea and Neotetanurae, near the base of Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Más tarde, Benson et al en 2010 encontraron que el clado Chuandongocoelurus y Monolophosaurus estaba fuera de Megalosauroidea y Neotetanurae, cerca de la base de Tetanurae.

facts.statement: Monolophosaurus lived during the Callovian stage, approximately 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)
